slices.title: Make the test suite immune to inherited GIT_* env (blocks the whole campaign)
slices.source: Found by the p6-mailer builder during the smoke test, then CONFIRMED BY REAL DAMAGE: the smoke run flipped core.bare=true on the main repo and broke `git status`.
slices.acceptance: With GIT_DIR/GIT_INDEX_FILE/GIT_WORK_TREE set to a foreign repo in the environment, the full suite still passes AND provably does not touch that repo (assert its config/HEAD/refs are byte-identical before and after).
slices.notes: MECHANISM, verified empirically: a pre-commit hook running inside a LINKED WORKTREE gets an absolute GIT_DIR=<main>/.git/worktrees/<name> and GIT_INDEX_FILE exported by git. .githooks/pre-commit runs `.venv/bin/pytest tests/ -q`, pytest inherits both, and GIT_DIR OVERRIDES cwd — so any test shelling out to git against a tmp_path repo is redirected onto the real repository. In a normal checkout GIT_DIR is unset, which is why this has never bitten before. DAMAGE OBSERVED: core.bare flipped to true on master, `git status` failed with 'this operation must be run in a work tree'. Refs and files survived; recovery was `git config core.bare false`. THE FIX MUST LIVE INSIDE PYTEST (a root tests/conftest.py, or the earliest-imported helper) — a scrub in the loop's gate script does NOT cover the hook path, because git invokes the hook itself. The repo has deliberately avoided a root conftest.py (see tests/json_handler/conftest.py's docstring); this is a good enough reason to add one that ONLY scrubs env.

slices.title: Process-group lifecycle: TERM grace then group KILL, bounded reaping, no unbounded communicate()
slices.acceptance: AppA M2 (L336): Process groups; bounded reap; orphan test
slices.notes: The executor kills only the direct child, orphaning MCP/hook/bash grandchildren. src/project_worker.py:88-89 does proc.kill() then communicate() with NO timeout — a pipe-holding grandchild hangs the worker forever and stalls its queue.

slices.title: Identity-checked process liveness: (pid, starttime, argv/cwd); exact /proc argv discovery replacing pgrep -f
slices.acceptance: AppA M3 (L337): (pid,starttime,argv) identity; PID-reuse simulation test. AppA M4 (L338): Exact argv match; metachar-path test.
slices.notes: Liveness is kill(pid,0) only (src/process_liveness.py:136-156, src/wake_helpers.py:20), so PID reuse yields phantom owners and unreaped rows. worker_manager.py:103-106 uses an UNESCAPED pgrep -f <path>, so any cmdline substring match becomes a phantom worker and blocks a real spawn.

slices.title: Server keypair in a dedicated GNUPGHOME (0600) so the backend can decrypt
slices.source: Amendment E2E — the server holds only a PUBLIC key today; decryption needs its own keypair
slices.acceptance: Server keypair exists in its own GNUPGHOME at 0600; the private key is absent from every spawned child's environment and from /proc/<pid>/environ
slices.exclude_reason: Blocked on the revised §11 spec and the app ack.
slices.notes: A spawned agent that can read this key can decrypt every command ever sent. Phase 2's env allowlist already excludes GPG_HOME — assert it explicitly for the new home too.

slices.title: Inbound: decrypt, then verify the INNER signature, then replay-check, then parse
slices.acceptance: Anything not encrypted is rejected at admission — plaintext, a bare multipart/signed, and any mixed/extra part. Identity comes from the inner signature only.
slices.notes: Sign-then-encrypt: the signature is INSIDE the ciphertext, so it is verified only after decryption. Nothing outside the ciphertext may influence what executes — this is why routing moved out of headers.

slices.title: Encrypt every outbound reply to the enrolled device and sign it with the server key
slices.source: Amendment E2E — answers D2, which had deferred reply encryption
slices.acceptance: No outbound body leaves in cleartext on ANY path: result, ack, error, status, relay. A test asserts every send path goes through the encrypting sender.
slices.notes: Four separate send paths exist today (send_threaded_reply, chat_relay, json_handler's _send_json_reply, and mailer.send_reply). Funnel them through one encrypting sender and assert it has a single caller, or a cleartext path creeps back.

slices.title: Protected headers: dummy outer Subject, real Subject inside the ciphertext
slices.acceptance: Outer Subject is a constant dummy carrying zero task information; the real Subject round-trips inside the encrypted part
slices.notes: SUPERSEDES the 'generated subjects from allowlisted correlation tags' half of p1-3-secret-leak — a correlation tag in a readable Subject still leaks task identity. Headers are the only remaining leak once bodies are encrypted, so minimise them.
